note: First prompt-driven judging run: the prompt assembled by `walkdown judge panel.viewport.device-presets`, the verdict earned by the agent driving its own browser. One rule, by design.

results.reasoning: Judged live in the framed layout on screen review with the fade at 50 so the ghost rendered throughout. The control reads as devices, not numbers: Fit is a word, desktop and mobile are icons with empty text, and the widths live only in the tooltips ("Desktop — lay the page out at 1440px", "Mobile — lay the page out at 390px"). Choosing mobile re-rendered both iframes at a true 390x664 with no transform — the stand-in re-flowed into a narrow column rather than shrinking a desktop rendering — and the corner badge read 390px. Switching to desktop restored both to a 1440px layout, each carrying the identical scale matrix(0.597222) to fit the 860px box, with the badge honestly saying "1440px · fit 60%". At every state measured, frame and ghost agreed exactly in CSS width, rect, and transform. One observation outside this rule's claim: the stand-in's own header wraps scruffily at 390 — that is the app's rendering, which the frame reported honestly, exactly its job. Panel state (Fit, fade 100) restored after judging; nothing was written.
